# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

# gba-emu build plan

Goal: an original Game Boy Advance emulator in Rust, built as `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, exporting the 10
functions in `gba-eval/spec/ABI.md`, that scores above the 0.534 baseline on the gba-eval grader. The
grader's highest reachable score is 0.96, because the `comprehensive` subsystem carries weight but has no tests.

Paths in this document are relative to this repo (`gba-trial/gba-emu`). The benchmark repo is
`/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.

## Scope: must-have vs stretch

| Phases | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | **Must-have** | Skeleton, CPU, interrupts/timers/DMA, full graphics. Each one finished, gated and verified with a milestone grade before the next starts. |
| 4-6 | **Stretch** | Sound, game compatibility/timing, performance. Started only once Phase 3 is verified, and dropped if time runs out. |

A solid, verified 0-3 is worth more than a broken 0-6. Never start a stretch phase while a
must-have gate is failing, and never leave `main` in a state that does not build or that scores lower
than the last milestone.

---

## 1. How the score is made (what to optimise)

| Section | Weight | Tests | Scoring |
|---|---|---|---|
| Replay | 60% | 11 homebrew games with recorded input | Mean per-frame SSIM vs Mesen2 over thousands of frames. Drifting out of sync ruins every later frame. |
| Procedural | 20% | 16 test ROMs | Only the final frame counts, and it must be almost pixel-exact (pass/fail). |
| Audio | 20% | 9 of the replays | Per-frame log-mel spectrum vs Mesen2. Silence scores 0. |

Procedural subsystem weights: cpu 0.35, comprehensive 0.20 (no tests, always 0), memory 0.15,
timer 0.12, halt_irq 0.10, dma 0.08. Audio: psg 0.5, game_audio 0.5.

Consequences:
- **CPU correctness comes first.** Every other test depends on it.
- **The PPU (graphics) carries the most weight**, because all 11 replays are graphics comparisons.
- **Timing accuracy matters a lot**, because replay inputs land on fixed frame numbers. If the game boots
  a few frames later than in Mesen2, every button press lands at the wrong moment.
- **Colour precision is forgiving.** The grader quantises to 5 bits per channel, so any sensible
  5-to-8-bit colour expansion is fine.

---

## 2. Architecture and shared contracts (Phase 0, one agent, before any parallel work)

Everything that more than one agent touches is defined here first. Parallel agents then work only inside
their own files, which is what keeps merges conflict-free.

One crate, `gba_emu`, with `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`. The `rlib` lets `cargo test` and a native
debug binary run on the host without wasm.

```
src/
  lib.rs          ABI exports only (the 10 functions), thin wrappers over a single global Gba
  gba.rs          Gba struct: owns every component, run_frame() main loop
  bus.rs          memory map: read8/16/32, write8/16/32, region dispatch, returns access cycles
  io.rs           IO register dispatch table: address range -> owning component
  irq.rs          IE / IF / IME, request(IrqSource), pending() -> bool
  scheduler.rs    cycle counter; components are stepped by "cycles elapsed"
  cpu/mod.rs      Cpu struct, register file, modes, banking, CPSR/SPSR, exceptions, step()
  cpu/alu.rs      barrel shifter, add/sub with flags, condition evaluation
  cpu/arm.rs      ARM (32-bit) decode + execute
  cpu/thumb.rs    THUMB (16-bit) decode + execute
  ppu/mod.rs      line timing, DISPCNT/DISPSTAT/VCOUNT, line compositor, framebuffer
  ppu/bg_text.rs  tiled backgrounds (modes 0-2)
  ppu/bg_affine.rs rotation/scaling backgrounds
  ppu/bitmap.rs   modes 3/4/5
  ppu/obj.rs      sprites (normal + affine)
  ppu/effects.rs  windows, blending, mosaic
  timer.rs        4 timers, prescaler, cascade, overflow IRQ, FIFO tick
  dma.rs          4 DMA channels, triggers, priority
  apu/mod.rs      mixer, SOUNDCNT/SOUNDBIAS, output buffer, sample rate
  apu/psg.rs      channels 1-4
  apu/fifo.rs     direct sound channels A/B
  keypad.rs       KEYINPUT / KEYCNT
  cart.rs         ROM, save memory (SRAM / Flash / EEPROM), GPIO
src/bin/run_rom.rs  native debug tool: run a ROM for N frames, write the frame as .ppm and audio as .wav
```

Contracts fixed in Phase 0:

1. **Bus.** `fn read32(&mut self, addr: u32) -> u32` and the other widths, plus a cycle cost for each
   access. The CPU only talks to the bus, never to components directly.
2. **IO registers.** `io.rs` maps address ranges to owners: PPU `0x000-0x05F`, APU `0x060-0x0AF`,

(64K+32K+32K, the two 32K blocks itself being mirrors of each other).
BIOS ROM, Normal ROM Cartridges, and I/O area are NOT mirrored, the only exception is the undocumented I/O port at 4000800h (repeated each 64K).
The 64K SRAM area is mirrored across the whole 32MB area at E000000h-FFFFFFFh, also, inside of the 64K SRAM field, 32K SRAM chips are repeated twice.

Writing 8bit Data to Video Memory
Video Memory (BG, OBJ, OAM, Palette) can be written to in 16bit and 32bit units only. Attempts to write 8bit data (by STRB opcode) won't work:
Writes to OBJ (6010000h-6017FFFh) (or 6014000h-6017FFFh in Bitmap mode) and to OAM (7000000h-70003FFh) are ignored, the memory content remains unchanged.
Writes to BG (6000000h-600FFFFh) (or 6000000h-6013FFFh in Bitmap mode) and to Palette (5000000h-50003FFh) are writing the new 8bit value to BOTH upper and lower 8bits of the addressed halfword, ie. "[addr AND NOT 1]=data*101h".

Using Invalid Tile Numbers
In Text mode, large tile numbers (combined with a non-zero character base setting in BGnCNT register) may exceed the available 64K of BG VRAM.
On GBA and GBA SP, such invalid tiles are displayed as if the character data is filled by the 16bit BG Map entry value (ie. as vertically striped tiles). Above applies only if there is only one BG layer enabled, with two or more layers, things are getting much more complicated: tile-data is then somehow derived from the other layers, depending on their priority order and scrolling offsets.
On NDS (in GBA mode), such invalid tiles are displayed as if the character data is zero-filled (ie. as invisible/transparent tiles).

Accessing SRAM Area by 16bit/32bit
Reading retrieves 8bit value from specified address, multiplied by 0101h (LDRH) or by 01010101h (LDR). Writing changes the 8bit value at the specified address only, being set to LSB of (source_data ROR (address*8)).

content.text:
I found no blockers. Six findings need fixing before or soon after merge: five minor, plus one major process gap.

- `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-ac23e34c0c2f986ed/src/gba.rs:21`: [major] `FRAME_END_LINE = 160` and the shorter first frame are guesses. PLAN.md §2 item 4 and §5 risk 3 say the frame boundary must be checked against Mesen2 in Phase 0. That check can't be done with a stub CPU, and NOTES.md (not touched by this branch) doesn't record the decision or that it was put off, which CLAUDE.md requires. Suggested fix: add a NOTES.md entry with the date, the choice and the reason, and make "check FRAME_END_LINE against the reference" an explicit Phase 1 gate task for the integrator.
- `src/bus.rs:167`, `:187`, `:220`, `:235`: [minor] 16- and 32-bit SRAM accesses use the address after it has been rounded down (`& !1` / `& !3`). gbatek, "Accessing SRAM Area by 16bit/32bit", says the read uses the byte at the exact address. The write changes only that byte, set to the low byte of `value ROR (address*8)`; the code writes the low byte unrotated. Suggested fix: handle SRAM before the rounding, using the original address and rotating the value for writes.
- `src/bus.rs:203` (write8, VRAM arm): [minor] 8-bit writes to the OBJ area (0x06010000-0x06017FFF, or from 0x06014000 in bitmap modes) should be ignored (gbatek "Writing 8bit Data to Video Memory"). Today they copy the byte into both halves. The `ponytail:` comment hands this to the PPU agent, but `bus.rs` is a shared file, so that agent can't fix it. Suggested fix: the integrator owns this; ask the PPU for the bitmap-mode boundary, or note it in PLAN.md.
- `src/bus.rs:246`: [minor] The undocumented register at 0x04000800 repeats every 64K (gbatek, next to the mirroring notes). `io_offset` only accepts the exact 0x800-0x803. Suggested fix: map `(offset & 0xFFFF)` in 0x800-0x803 for any offset of 0x400 or more. This is low priority.
- `src/ppu/mod.rs:178`: [minor] Writing a new LYC value in DISPSTAT doesn't re-check the VCOUNT match flag. At power-on (VCOUNT 0, LYC 0) the flag also stays clear until line 0 comes round again. Suggested fix: call `update_vcount_match` after a DISPSTAT write, without raising the IRQ there if timing tests disagree, and set the flag in `new()`.
- `src/bus.rs:262`: [minor] Readability: the `fold` one-liner with shifts is denser than the rest of the file. Suggested fix: use the existing `read_le16`/`read_le32` helpers on `BIOS` after the bounds check.
- `src/irq.rs:90`: [minor] Readability: the mask `0xFF00` means "the HALTCNT byte was written", but nothing says so. Suggested fix: add a named constant such as `HALTCNT_BYTE_MASK` with a comment.

**Spec checks that came out right:** the DISPSTAT flags (VBlank on lines 160-226, HBlank on every line at cycle 1006, writable mask 0xFF38), the VRAM mirror (0x18000-0x1FFFF repeats 0x10000-0x17FFF), palette byte writes going to both halves, OAM ignoring byte writes, the default wait states (EWRAM 3/6, ROM 5/8, SRAM 5), the IF write-1-to-clear, the CPU reset state (Supervisor mode, IRQ and FIQ masked), the KEYINPUT bit order, and the sample rate `32768 << SOUNDBIAS[15:14]`.

**Ownership:** Phase 0 owns all of section 2, so this is fine. The only files outside that table are `.cargo/config.toml` (a `cargo wasm` alias), `Cargo.lock` and `assets/gba_bios_stub.bin`. The BIOS file is byte-identical to the `$GBA_EVAL/spec` copy, and keeping it in the repo avoids relative-path problems inside worktrees. Nothing in the diff branches on ROM identity.

**Tests:** I ran everything in `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-ac23e34c0c2f986ed`.
- `cargo test`: 6 of 6 pass. They cover bus round-trips, mirrors, BIOS being read-only, IF byte acknowledge, access cycles, frame alignment and the VBlank IRQ.
- Wasm build: no warnings, and `emu_boot_frames` is not exported.
- Smoke set (`aw-arm-alu`, `aw-thumb-alu`, `memory`, `timer-reload`, `dma-priority`, `tonc-snd1`): all about 0, as expected with a stub CPU. None was skipped as "trapped", so the Phase 0 gate passes.
